title: 'No other option': Excerpts of Putin's speech declaring war
claim: Putin framed the February 24 invasion as a necessary security move, warned that a direct attack on Russia would bring catastrophic consequences, and said Ukraine should not be allowed to acquire nuclear weapons.
source_confidence_reason: Direct transcript excerpt published the day of the invasion, translated from the Kremlin recording.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributed to Putin as the speaking president.
contrary_evidence: The speech is self-justifying propaganda, not an independent account of the war's causes.

title: Путин поручил Минобороны РФ обеспечить поддержание мира в ДНР и ЛНР
claim: Putin's recognition decrees for the self-proclaimed DPR and LPR said Ukraine had refused peaceful settlement under the Minsk agreements and ordered the Russian military to perform peacekeeping functions there.
source_confidence_reason: Russian-language publication of the decree text on the day it was signed.
ruler_attribution: Direct presidential decree attributable to Putin.
contrary_evidence: The decrees were widely treated internationally as a prelude to aggression rather than peacekeeping.

title: Russia reframes war goals as Ukrainians advance near Kyiv
claim: Reuters reported that Moscow was scaling back its ambitions in Ukraine after setbacks near Kyiv and shifting focus to the eastern Donbass region.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting on the Russian side's change in stated military aims.
ruler_attribution: Reflects Putin's war policy as implemented by the Russian state.
contrary_evidence: The article describes a military adjustment after failure, not a genuine peace settlement.

title: Итоги российско-украинских переговоров в Стамбуле. Главное
claim: Kommersant reported that Russia said it would reduce military activity on the Kyiv and Chernihiv fronts after the Istanbul talks and had received Ukrainian written proposals on neutrality and security guarantees.
source_confidence_reason: Russian-language contemporaneous summary of the talks and Russian claims about de-escalation.
period_fit: Directly in the March 2022 negotiation window.
ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Russian negotiating position under Putin.
contrary_evidence: The reduction was framed as conditional and reversible, not a durable ceasefire.

title: Russian Federation: Authorities impose censorship on media and crush peaceful anti-war protests following invasion of Ukraine
claim: Roskomnadzor ordered media to rely only on official Russian sources for invasion coverage and threatened sanctions for spreading false information, effectively imposing censorship.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights organization statement with specific legal and regulatory details.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Putin’s state apparatus because Roskomnadzor acted as the official media watchdog under his government.
contrary_evidence: Russian authorities framed the measure as preventing false information about the war.

title: Russia: Kremlin’s ruthless crackdown stifles independent journalism and anti-war movement
claim: Amnesty said Russian authorities blocked independent media, banned Facebook and Twitter, and had arbitrarily arrested more than 13,800 people at anti-war rallies since 24 February 2022.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous NGO reporting with concrete arrest and censorship figures.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Putin’s government because the crackdown was implemented by state authorities and Roskomnadzor/police.
contrary_evidence: Authorities described the war and restrictions as necessary responses to the invasion and misinformation.

title: We publish a report on political prisoners and political repression in Russia in 2022
claim: Memorial said repression of public dissent reached unprecedented levels in 2022, political opposition was effectively outlawed, independent media were shut down, censorship was institutionalized, protest activity was suppressed, and the number of political prisoners reached 513 by the end of 2022.
source_confidence_reason: Major Russian rights project summarizing its own monitored casework and year-end counts.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Putin’s regime because the report describes state repression, censorship, and police-force conduct in 2022.
contrary_evidence: This is an advocacy-monitoring report and is retrospective rather than contemporaneous.

title: Политзаключённые и политические репрессии в России в 2022 году
claim: Memorial said 2022 was marked by de facto military censorship, 74 new names were added to the main political-prisoner list, and more than 5,000 administrative cases and 200-plus criminal cases targeted anti-army speech.
source_confidence_reason: Local-language retrospective report with explicit annual statistics and repression categories.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Putin’s regime because the report describes state repression in response to anti-war speech and public dissent.
contrary_evidence: The report is a retrospective summary and not a contemporaneous government record.

title: Putin tells Russian business people he had no choice over Ukraine
claim: Putin told Russian business leaders that he had no choice but to order the operation against Ukraine and framed the war as a forced decision.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters is a high-quality wire service; the claim reports Putin's own remarks contemporaneously.
ruler_attribution: direct speech by Putin, fully attributable to him
contrary_evidence: Later reporting showed the invasion was a deliberate strategic choice, not an unavoidable necessity.

title: Ukraine urges halt to Russia's assault as Biden heads to Poland
claim: Reuters reported that Moscow was scaling back its ambitions after setbacks near Kyiv and shifting focus to the eastern Donbass region.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters is a strong contemporaneous news source and the article reports observable battlefield/strategy changes.
ruler_attribution: Putin ultimately controlled the war strategy, though the shift also reflected military setbacks and subordinate implementation.
contrary_evidence: The article also reflects pressure from battlefield failure rather than voluntary strategic refinement.

title: Kommersant reports Russia will reduce military activity on Kyiv and Chernihiv fronts after Istanbul talks
claim: Russia said it would reduce military activity on the Kyiv and Chernihiv fronts after the Istanbul talks and had received Ukrainian written proposals on neutrality.
source_confidence_reason: Domestic reporting is useful for the statement and chronology, though it is less independent than international wire reporting.
ruler_attribution: Putin's government controlled the negotiation posture and military response, but the move was also shaped by battlefield conditions.
contrary_evidence: Whether this was a genuine de-escalation or a tactical redeployment remained disputed.

title: Putin orders new budget rules to boost Russia's growth
claim: Putin ordered new budget rules and said they should ensure stability of public finances and raise growth rates.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters reports a concrete policy directive from Putin tied to fiscal management and growth goals.
ruler_attribution: directly attributable to Putin as head of state ordering the policy change
contrary_evidence: The article does not itself prove effective implementation, only intent and formal direction.

title: Russia's Putin proposes to reappoint central bank chief Nabiullina
claim: Putin proposed reappointing Elvira Nabiullina and Reuters reported that the move was framed as helping preserve macroeconomic stability.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters is a strong source for the appointment and the public rationale attached to it.
ruler_attribution: direct appointment power by Putin over a key economic official
contrary_evidence: The central bank retained some operational autonomy, so competence credit is only partial and mediated.

title: Russia increases its emergency spending fund by $46b
claim: Russia increased its emergency spending fund to support economic stability under sanctions and had already pledged more than 1 trillion roubles in anti-crisis support to businesses.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting, republished by a major outlet, describes a concrete fiscal response to sanctions shock.
ruler_attribution: Putin's government controlled the fiscal response, though execution also depended on ministries and the budget system.
contrary_evidence: The move reflects crisis defense under duress rather than a clean growth expansion.

title: Russia economy: pensions
claim: Putin called for an 8.6% pension increase above inflation and had previously ordered one-off social payments and public-sector salary hikes worth at least 500 billion roubles.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting captures a specific budget and distribution choice attributed to Putin.
ruler_attribution: directly attributable to Putin's policy choice and public instruction
contrary_evidence: The measure may have been partly compensatory because inflation was already running above plan.

title: Putin orders benefit payments for people arriving in Russia from Ukraine
claim: Putin signed a decree creating monthly pension payments and other benefits for people forced to leave Ukrainian territory for Russia.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters reports a signed decree and the benefit structure, which are directly observable policy actions.
ruler_attribution: directly attributable to Putin's decree authority, though implementation ran through state agencies.
contrary_evidence: This is a targeted wartime benefit and does not show broad welfare improvement.

title: Russia economy: Putin forum
claim: Putin said Russia would post a budget surplus in 2022, forecast GDP would fall around 2 percent, and acknowledged that economic hardships remained for many Russians.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting captures Putin's public macroeconomic claims and expectations in September 2022.
ruler_attribution: direct public positioning by Putin, though the actual macro path depended on the central bank, finance ministry, war, and sanctions.
contrary_evidence: Later data showed a more mixed picture than the optimistic framing suggested.

title: Russian unemployment rate hits record low, economic data paints mixed picture
claim: Russia's unemployment fell to a record low of 3.8 percent, but real wages fell 3.2 percent year on year in July and car production dropped 69 percent.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters is a strong source for contemporaneous economic outcomes reported from official data.
ruler_attribution: outcomes were only partly attributable to Putin because they also reflected sanctions, war disruption, and central bank actions.
contrary_evidence: Low unemployment coexisted with falling wages and severe sectoral contraction.

title: Russia's 2022 economic fall seen in lower incomes, slumping consumer demand
claim: Reuters reported Rosstat data showing real disposable incomes fell 1 percent in 2022, retail sales slumped 6.7 percent, and consumer demand contracted sharply.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters is strong for reporting official statistical releases and the article gives specific year-end outcomes.
ruler_attribution: mixed attribution: Putin's war and sanctions policy mattered, but so did external sanctions and household behavior.
contrary_evidence: The same article noted some labor-market resilience, so the downturn was uneven rather than absolute.

title: Russia says budget deficit hit 2.3% of GDP in 2022
claim: Reuters reported that Russia recorded a 2022 budget deficit of 2.3 percent of GDP and had to draw on its rainy-day fund while diverting more money toward security and defense.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters is a strong source for the fiscal outcome and the allocation tradeoff.
period_fit: retrospective evidence about the 2022 target period
ruler_attribution: Putin's war and spending priorities were central, but the fiscal outcome also reflected sanctions and energy prices.
contrary_evidence: The deficit was manageable by sovereign standards, so this is a mixed rather than catastrophic signal.

title: Bank of Russia raises key rate because inflation was above forecast
claim: The central bank raised the key rate because inflation was above forecast and demand was outpacing output capacity.
source_confidence_reason: Primary official monetary-policy statement with explicit rationale and date.
ruler_attribution: indirect: the Bank of Russia acted under its own mandate, though the broader policy environment was shaped by Putin's state
contrary_evidence: This reflects central-bank autonomy, so it cannot be credited fully to Putin alone.

title: Bank of Russia hikes key rate to 20% to support financial and price stability
claim: The Bank of Russia hiked the key rate to 20 percent to support financial and price stability and protect household savings from depreciation.
source_confidence_reason: Primary official policy action with explicit target and rationale.
ruler_attribution: indirect to Putin; this was executed by the central bank rather than by presidential decree alone.
contrary_evidence: The need for such an emergency hike shows severe shock rather than clean success.

title: Central bank says 28 February hike and capital controls helped support stable functioning of financial system
claim: The central bank said the late-February rate hike and capital controls helped support the stable functioning of the financial system.
source_confidence_reason: Primary official statement directly linking policy tools to observed stabilization.
ruler_attribution: mostly indirect to Putin because the bank carried out the stabilization, though it operated inside his regime's wartime policy framework.
contrary_evidence: Stabilization was defensive and partial, not proof of broad economic success.

title: Bank of Russia monetary policy 2022-2024
claim: The Bank of Russia stated that price stability close to 4 percent is its main goal and that forecast-based decisions and transparency are core monetary-policy principles.
source_confidence_reason: Primary policy framework document from the central bank.
ruler_attribution: indirect to Putin; this documents the institutional framework rather than a personal directive.
contrary_evidence: Institutional principles do not prove that Putin himself governed competently.

title: Russia's domestic economy had been doing fairly well because emergency financial and monetary measures helped stabilize the financial sector
claim: The IMF said Russia's domestic economy had been doing fairly well because emergency financial and monetary measures helped stabilize the financial sector, even though the projected medium-term outlook remained weak.
source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF transcript from a formal public briefing, directly summarizing the macro response and its limits.
ruler_attribution: mixed: the stabilization reflected both Putin's wartime policy environment and the central bank's emergency measures.
contrary_evidence: The IMF also emphasized that the medium-term outlook remained weak.

title: IMF staff statement on the economic impact of war in Ukraine
claim: The IMF said sanctions on the Russian Central Bank would severely restrict access to reserves and disrupt cross-border transactions, and it urged fiscal policy to support the most vulnerable.
source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF statement contemporaneous with the sanctions shock.
ruler_attribution: indirect to Putin; this is an external constraint created by his war policy and the international response.
contrary_evidence: The statement is about constraints and advice, not proof of Putin's competence or incompetence by itself.

title: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2022 Issue 2
claim: The OECD said sanctions cut Russia off from foreign capital and reserves, the ruble depreciated sharply, the policy rate rose to 20 percent, and the downturn could be larger than earlier expected.
source_confidence_reason: Major international institution synthesis using cross-country macro data and policy analysis.
ruler_attribution: mixed: Putin's war decision created the shock, but the OECD's focus is on the combined effects of sanctions and policy response.
contrary_evidence: The OECD text shows that external sanctions were a major driver, not only Putin's internal management.

title: ECB Financial Stability Review, May 2022
claim: The ECB said sanctions had significantly isolated Russia's economy and were reflected in a sharp downgrade of its growth outlook and higher inflation expectations.
source_confidence_reason: Primary central-bank analysis from a major international institution.
ruler_attribution: indirect to Putin because the shock was produced by the war and sanctions environment around him.
contrary_evidence: This source is a macro-risk analysis, not a direct measure of Putin's own execution quality.

title: Russia economy: Putin forum

source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting captures a public macro forecast and self-assessment from Putin.
ruler_attribution: direct public claim by Putin, though outcome depended on sanctions, central-bank actions, and war spending.
contrary_evidence: Later year-end data showed a more mixed and weaker household picture than the rhetoric suggested.

title: Russia says budget deficit hit 2.3% of GDP in 2022
claim: Reuters reported that Russia recorded a 2022 budget deficit of 2.3 percent of GDP and had to draw on its rainy-day fund while diverting more resources toward security and defense.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters is a strong source for the fiscal outcome and the tradeoff between stabilization and military spending.
period_fit: retrospective evidence about the 2022 target period
ruler_attribution: Putin's war and spending priorities were central, though the fiscal result also reflected sanctions and commodity conditions.
contrary_evidence: The deficit remained manageable, so this is a mixed rather than decisive failure signal.

claim: Putin signed the law approving the 2022 federal budget execution report; it records 27.824 trillion rubles in revenue, 31.119 trillion rubles in spending, and a 3.295 trillion ruble deficit.

ruler_attribution: direct presidential approval of the budget execution law, though execution was carried by the wider fiscal apparatus
contrary_evidence: The result was a deficit, not the budget balance implied by the original 2022 plan.

ruler_attribution: directly attributable to Putin's command authority over the cabinet and security ministries
contrary_evidence: This is strong evidence of mobilization and planning, but not yet proof of durable delivery by year-end.
